svg.title: The two Thom maps transfer a negative two-jet measure trace
svg.desc: For every x in K zero of A two, the additive positive-loop Thom map and Morita map give y in K one of A one with raw J psi of y equal to T two of x. The increasing-frequency odd Thom map and second Morita map give z in K zero of A with raw J tau of z equal to minus T two of x divided by two pi i. Their composite is the direct principal-bundle Morita map after the ordered two-step Thom map. Multiplying the final raw pairing by two pi i transfers the negative measure minus two nu. Section 12 proves the global class and measured index; the proper-cycle Thom comparison remains open.
svg.metadata: Original mathematical diagram, CC0. Theorem 11.2 and Corollary 11.3.
svg.text: Two real Thom maps, with their raw pairing constants
A₂ = C₀(J₂⁺(S¹)) ⋊ᵣ Γ, A₁ = C₀(J₁⁺(S¹)) ⋊ᵣ Γ, A = C(S¹) ⋊ᵣ Γ
Fourier transform: ∫ f(t)exp(itξ) dt, ξ increases
β ∧ dβ = −2ν in the jet coordinates
Global class and measured index: Section 12.
The proper-cycle Thom comparison is still open.
All K-classes, matrices, nonunital algebras and arbitrary discrete Γ.
Proofs: Theorem 11.2; Corollary 11.3; Sections 7–10. Human source: Connes, transverse class, §7.
